# Every number below is read from the tables the manuscript writes, so the letter cannot disagree with the paper.
strip <- read.csv("../03.outputs/statewide_strip.csv"); area <- read.csv("../03.outputs/statewide_area.csv"); regions <- read.csv("../03.outputs/statewide_regions.csv", row.names = 1)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f", 100 * x); share <- function(nm) pct(area$susceptible_km2[area$region == nm] / area$forest_km2[area$region == nm])

`r format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y")`

The Editor
Ecological Indicators

Dear Editor,

I am pleased to submit "A spruce beetle susceptibility map of Alaska using Sentinel-1 radar and crown-scale mortality data in the Susitna valley" for consideration as an original research article in Ecological Indicators.

Spruce beetle outbreaks in Alaska kill the largest spruce first, so the tallest stands of large spruce are the ones most at risk in the next outbreak. Managers rate that hazard from stand measurements on the ground, which cannot be made across a state, and no study had tested whether radar measures of stand structure pick out the stands an outbreak kills. The manuscript makes that test and then maps the stands across Alaska.

Scored against the crown-scale map of the spruce the current outbreak had killed in the Susitna valley by 2021, `r format(strip$n, big.mark = ",")` cells of 90 m, the pre-outbreak Sentinel-1 backscatter classed `r pct(strip$sens_VV)` per cent of the killed stands and `r pct(strip$spec_VV)` per cent of the spared stands correctly, an overall accuracy of `r pct(strip$acc_VV)` per cent. Pooled across every scene over Alaska, it gave a 90 m map covering `r format(round(area$forest_km2[area$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = ",")` km² of forest, `r share("alaska")` per cent of it at or above the threshold, which ranked attacked above unattacked forest in the aerial detection survey on the Kenai Peninsula and in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough and failed in the open woodland of the Copper River basin, where the canopy height map ranked them instead.

The map is an indicator of stand susceptibility that a manager can read before the beetle arrives. It is a public Google Earth Engine asset, and every number in the manuscript is computed from code shown in the manuscript, so the indicator can be rebuilt or extended.

The manuscript is original, has not been published and is not under consideration elsewhere. I am the sole author. I have no competing interests to declare, and the work received no funding.

Yours sincerely,

Seamus Robert Murphy
seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com
